  "text": "Tobias Reel came down from the church when the bell had gone for morning and the tide was where a tide should be.\n\nThere were gulls. He counted them without meaning to, the way he counted posts. The wind had come back from the north and it smelled of nothing but salt.\n\nHe went along the top of the dune and did not go down to the water. From there he could see the house. The door was shut. He could not say whether he was glad of it.\n\nThe lamp stood in the front window on the sill where she kept it. It was not lit. In daylight that was nothing; nobody lit a lamp at this hour. He looked at it longer than he needed to all the same.\n\nOn the beach the eleven posts stood up out of the wet sand in their line, her father's work, leaning the way they had always leaned. The sea had left a dark mark on each of them at the same height. He had seen high-water marks all his life. This one was higher than the tide had any cause to be, and it was level, and it was dry already.\n\nHe did not go to the door. He had never once in forty years gone to that door uninvited, and he found he could not think of a reason that would hold.\n\nBehind him the bell gave its last note. He turned toward it. He walked up the hill, and he did not look back, and that was the only part of it he had ever been sure of.",
